period: Traditionally placed in the 9th century CE.
context: Vasugupta is honoured in Kashmir Shaivism as the one to whom the Shiva Sutras were revealed. Tradition relates that the sutras were disclosed to him in a dream by Shiva and found inscribed on a rock on Mahadeva mountain; this account is legendary. The Shiva Sutras became a foundational text of the non-dual Shaiva traditions of Kashmir. The Spanda Karikas, which develop the idea of consciousness as dynamic vibration, are attributed either to him or to his disciple Kallata.
coreIdeas: Consciousness is the Self, and the Self is Shiva
The world arises as the free expression of Shiva's consciousness and power (shakti)
Bondage is a limitation of knowledge that contracts universal consciousness into the individual
Liberation is realised through different means (upayas), from effortless insight to disciplined practice
Consciousness is inherently dynamic (spanda), not inert
otherWorks: Spanda Karikas (attributed either to Vasugupta or to his disciple Kallata)
attributionNote: The Shiva Sutras are considered revealed, with Vasugupta as recipient. Authorship of the Spanda Karikas is debated between Vasugupta and Kallata.
